sentences: Trees cannot walk or run, but a new study shows that they can still **sense** their own shape and fix it.
Researchers at INRAE, a research institute in France, grew young **poplar** trees on their side, and after about ten days the stems began to **curve** upward.
The scientists then put the trees on a slowly turning platform, so that light and **gravity** could no longer tell them which way was up.
Even so, the curved stems became almost straight again over the following weeks, which suggests that trees can feel the shape of their own bodies.
en.answer: 나무는 걷거나 뛸 수 없지만, 새 연구에 따르면 나무도 자기 모양을 감지하고 바로잡을 수 있다.

sentences: Am 11. November feiern viele Kinder in Deutschland den **Martinstag**, der an den heiligen Martin von Tours erinnert.
Nach einer bekannten **Legende** teilte Martin an einem kalten Abend seinen Mantel mit einem armen Mann, der fror.
Schon Wochen vorher basteln die Kinder im Kindergarten oder in der Schule bunte **Laternen** aus Papier und Pappe.
Wenn es dunkel wird, ziehen sie mit ihren Eltern durch die Straßen und singen dabei traditionelle **Martinslieder**.
de.answer: 11월 11일에 독일의 많은 아이들은 투르의 성 마르틴을 기리는 마르틴 축일을 기념합니다.
words: 마르틴 축일에 부르는 노래 (중성 das, 복수 Martinslieder)
